description: A deputy general counsel must approve the company's litigation strategy in a patent-infringement case, including which patent claims to pursue, the scope of technical discovery, and protections for source code, with input from patent litigation counsel and the company's technology liaison.

shared_context.S1: The company has been sued for infringement of two issued software-patent claims, identified in the complaint as claim 7 and claim 12.
shared_context.S2: The first case-management conference is scheduled for three weeks from today.
shared_context.S3: The current draft litigation plan preserves both claims, seeks broad technical discovery, and permits source-code production under the opposing party's proposed protective order.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's standard pre-conference review, Elena asks patent litigation counsel and the technology liaison to report any facts that should change the draft plan before she approves it.
shared_context.S5: If a claim is shown to be anticipated in full, the litigation plan should withdraw that claim from the asserted-claims strategy rather than continue pursuing it, and discovery should be limited to material relevant to any surviving claim.

PF1.text: While reviewing a newly indexed prior-art collection yesterday, Thomas found a published 2016 software implementation that anticipates every limitation of claim 7. Under the team's litigation policy, this requires claim 7 to be withdrawn from the asserted-claims strategy; his separate review found no equivalent anticipation of claim 12. He has not revised the draft plan because the prior-art collection was indexed after the plan circulated.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed with the engineering security team this week that the proposed protective order is inadequate for the company's source code: it allows two named employees of the opposing party to access produced code. The company's board-approved security policy requires source-code access to be limited to outside counsel and independent experts who have signed enhanced source-code acknowledgments, and Nadia has not yet updated the litigation plan because the security team's confirmation arrived after the last legal-team meeting.

acceptance_conditions: The company must pursue claim 12 but not claim 7.
Claim 7 must be withdrawn from the asserted-claims strategy.
Discovery must exclude claim-7-only material and focus on material relevant to claim 12.
Source-code production must be conditioned on a modified protective order.
Source-code access must be limited to outside counsel and independent experts.
Enhanced source-code acknowledgments must be required before any source-code production.
The claim-strategy revision must be recorded as a commitment.
The prior-art finding must be cited by the decision-maker as justification for withdrawing claim 7.
The security finding must be cited by the decision-maker as justification for the source-code protections.

content_checks.C1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'claim_12' in decisions['claims_to_pursue'] and 'claim_7' not in decisions['claims_to_pursue']
content_checks.C6: 'PF1' in revealed and any(c['type'] == 'claim_analysis_revision' or c['type'] == 'plan_revision' or c['type'] == 'strategy_revision' or c['type'] == 'claim_strategy_revision' or c['type'] == 'deliverable' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The 2016 implementation anticipates every limitation of claim 7, changing the asserted strategy from preserving both claims to pursuing only claim 12, withdrawing claim 7, and excluding claim-7-only discovery.

The security team's confirmation changes source-code production from the proposed order allowing two opposing-party employees to access code to a modified order allowing only outside counsel and independent experts with enhanced acknowledgments.
